newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares lower in bourse trade, dollar weighs.
newsitem.headline: German shares lower in bourse trade, dollar weighs.

text.p: German shares were lower in bourse trade on Thursday as a lower dollar weighed on the market and traders ignored an overnight record close on Wall Street.
"We've come to expect new records on Wall Street," said one Frankfurt trader.
The DAX index of 30 leading shares was down 5.30 points, or 0.19 percent, at 2,769.20 in midsession dealings, little moved after the German Bundesbank left interest rates unchanged.
"The Street was good, the weaker dollar is bad, so that comes out as pretty neutral," said one trader.
The dollar fell below the crucial 1.50 mark level on Wednesday after floor trade had closed.

Volumes were generally thin, with interest even limited in newly-floated Deutsche Telekom shares, with just under three million shares changing hands in bourse dealings, significantly less than in previous days.
Telekom was slightly firmer than the rest of the market, adding two pfennigs to trade at 31.82 pfennigs, with dealers saying profit-taking on the stock was petering out.

Shares in industrial group Daimler-Benz AG were also firmer, gaining 35 pfennigs to 97.15 marks, after interest in the company following an interview with the company's chairman in a German business magazine.
Chairman Juergen Schrempp said he expected 1996 group sales growth of 10 to 11 percent.
Shares in electronics firm Siemens AG were up 38 pfennigs at 72.25 marks, after the company announced a rise in 1995/96 after-tax profit of 29 million marks.

Meanwhile steel manufacturer Thyssen was weaker than the rest of the market, slipping 6.50 marks to 277 marks, with dealers saying some players were worried ahead of the firm's publication of 1995/96 results on Friday.
The stock had recently been climing on speculation that the firm would soon restructure.
